verdict.rationale: DBOS queues provide flow control that limits how many workflows run at once (concurrency caps) and how often workflows are started (rate limits), which covers per-queue and per-workflow throttling. Nothing in the evidence shows per-key or per-tenant partitioning, which is the part of the story that stops one hot customer from starving the rest. A Hatchet co-founder's concern about global rate-limit coordination is skepticism, not a concrete failure, so it lowers confidence only. Missing for 10: per-key or per-tenant concurrency and rate-limit partitioning, detailed docs on limit configuration, and independent hands-on corroboration of fairness under load.
